audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua Manasseh inheritance, Zelophehad's daughters, Canaanite persistence, and Joseph-tribe complaint, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Machir/Gilead, clan allotments, Zelophehad's daughters receiving inheritance, Manasseh boundary/enclave complexity, non-dispossessed Canaanites, forced labor, Joseph's complaint, forest-clearing, and iron-chariot rhetoric.

verses.restored: Lot came for tribe of Manasseh, for he was firstborn of Joseph; for Machir firstborn of Manasseh, father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, Gilead and Bashan were his.

familiar.text: There was also a lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the firstborn of Joseph; to wit, for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead: because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

modern.text: Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh as Joseph’s firstborn son, namely for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh and father of the Gileadites, who had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י הַגּוֹרָל֙ לְמַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּי ה֖וּא בְּכ֣וֹר יוֹסֵ֑ף לְמָכִיר֩ בְּכ֨וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲבִ֣י הַגִּלְעָ֗ד כִּ֣י ה֤וּא הָיָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיְהִי ל֖וֹ הַגִּלְעָ֥ד וְהַבָּשָֽׁן

verses.restored: There was also for remaining sons of Manasseh according to their clans: sons of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida; these were male children of Manasseh son of Joseph according to their clans.

familiar.text: There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families; for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph by their families.

modern.text: So this allotment was for the rest of the descendants of Manasseh—the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These are the other male descendants of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph.

original.text: וַ֠יְהִי לִבְנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה הַנּוֹתָרִים֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִבְנֵ֨י אֲבִיעֶ֜זֶר וְלִבְנֵי חֵ֗לֶק וְלִבְנֵ֤י אַשְׂרִיאֵל֙ וְלִבְנֵי שֶׁ֔כֶם וְלִבְנֵי חֵ֖פֶר וְלִבְנֵ֣י שְׁמִידָ֑ע אֵ֠לֶּה בְּנֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֧ה בֶּן יוֹסֵ֛ף הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם

verses.restored: But Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh had no sons, only daughters; these were names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

familiar.text: But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

modern.text: But Zelophehad son of Hepher (the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh) had no sons but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

original.text: וְלִצְלָפְחָד֩ בֶּן חֵ֨פֶר בֶּן גִּלְעָ֜ד בֶּן מָכִ֣יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה לֹא הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם בָּנ֑וֹת וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֹתָ֔יו מַחְלָ֣ה וְנֹעָ֔ה חָגְלָ֥ה מִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה

verses.restored: They drew near before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and leaders, saying, YHWH commanded Moses to give us inheritance among our brothers. So according to mouth of YHWH he gave them inheritance among brothers of their father.

familiar.text: And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren. Therefore according to the commandment of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

modern.text: They approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers, in keeping with the command of the LORD.

original.text: וַתִּקְרַ֡בְנָה לִפְנֵי֩ אֶלְעָזָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֗וּן וְלִפְנֵ֤י הַנְּשִׂיאִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶת מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָֽתֶת לָ֥נוּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ אַחֵ֑ינוּ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם אֶל פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ נַֽחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֥י אֲבִיהֶֽן

familiar.text: And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side Jordan;

modern.text: Thus ten shares fell to Manasseh, in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan,

original.text: וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חַבְלֵֽי מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה לְבַ֞ד מֵאֶ֤רֶץ הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְהַבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן

familiar.text: Because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh’s sons had the land of Gilead.

modern.text: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. And the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.

original.text: כִּ֚י בְּנ֣וֹת מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה נָחֲל֥וּ נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ בָּנָ֑יו וְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה לִבְנֵֽי מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה הַנּֽוֹתָרִֽים

verses.restored: Border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which is before Shechem; border went rightward to inhabitants of En-tappuah.

familiar.text: And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of Entappuah.

modern.text: Now the border of Manasseh went from Asher to Michmethath near Shechem, then southward to include the inhabitants of En-tappuah.

familiar.text: Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim;

modern.text: The region of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to Ephraim.

original.text: לִמְנַשֶּׁ֕ה הָיְתָ֖ה אֶ֣רֶץ תַּפּ֑וּחַ וְתַפּ֛וּחַ אֶל גְּב֥וּל מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Border went down to wadi Kanah, south of wadi; these cities belonged to Ephraim among cities of Manasseh. Border of Manasseh was north of wadi, and its end was sea.

familiar.text: And the coast descended unto the river Kanah, southward of the river: these cities of Ephraim are among the cities of Manasseh: the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea:

modern.text: From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah. There were cities belonging to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh, but the border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook and ended at the Sea.

familiar.text: Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border; and they met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east.

modern.text: Ephraim’s territory was to the south, and Manasseh’s was to the north, having the Sea as its border and adjoining Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

familiar.text: And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Bethshean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and her towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and her towns, even three countries.

modern.text: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh was assigned Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor (that is, Naphath), Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, each with their surrounding settlements.

modern.text: But the descendants of Manasseh were unable to occupy these cities, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in this land.

modern.text: However, when the Israelites grew stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor; but they failed to drive them out completely.

verses.restored: Children of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, Why have you given me inheritance of one lot and one portion, though I am a numerous people, since until now YHWH has blessed me?

modern.text: Then the sons of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance? We have many people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly.”

familiar.text: And Joshua answered them, If thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee.

modern.text: Joshua answered them, “If you have so many people that the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim.”

modern.text: “The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied, “and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel.”

translation_notes: The daughters of Zelophehad—Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah—successfully invoke YHWH's command through Moses and receive inheritance among their father's brothers.
Their appearance continues the gender-inheritance correction from Numbers 27 and 36 and should be read as women's legal agency within a still-patriarchal land system.
Manasseh's allotment includes overlapping and enclave-like arrangements with Ephraim, Issachar, and Asher, showing that tribal geography is not a neat modern map.
The text admits Canaanites remained in several cities and were determined to dwell there, contradicting total-erasure rhetoric.
Israel's later strength produces forced labor rather than equal coexistence. This is coercive domination, not justice.
Joshua's forest-clearing answer links inheritance to labor, but the command still ends with dispossessing strong Canaanite communities with iron chariots.
The chapter's land claim must not be used for modern displacement, forced labor, or denial of surviving communities' rights.
safety_note: Do not use Joshua 17 to justify displacement, forced labor, ethnic domination, or treating unresolved land pressure as permission to remove current inhabitants. Center the daughters of Zelophehad as legal agents, the text's admission of mixed populations, and the ethical need for inheritance without exploitation.
